newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end week just below record high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end week just below record high.

text.p: French shares closed at a fresh historic record close, just below an alltime intra-day trading high, as the market continued its bull run started on January 2 which is fuelled by fresh liquidities and a firmer dollar.
Special factors such as big rises in blue chips LVMH and Canal Plus also underpinned the index
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.33 points or 0.72 percent at 2,425.10 and set an all time high at 2,426.13.
The index gained 4.2 percent this week.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,429 from 2,408 on Thursday's close.
* Total volume was 9.97 billion francs, including foreign shares, among which 6.56 billion francs in blue-chip shares.
"The market is fundamentally bullish. There is an enormous wave of buying," a trader said, noting a lot of basket deals by funds that follow the CAC-40 index.

"The market wants to rise. New York is busy breaking new record and so are we," another trader said. "There is a lot of volume, loads of cash is being invested and that is going to continue," he said.
But the higher the market gets the more some players are getting nervous about a possible downward correction.
* This uncertainty fuels a string of market rumours which carry hopes corporate deals could further boost price levels.
"There is a restless search for new ideas to rise and the moment there is something to chew on the market goes for it," a trader said.
And some market rumours prove to be right.

* Havas on Thursday evening announced it was going to buy out minorities in its 74 percent unit CEP Communication for 407 francs per share, or 2.7 billion francs. Havas shares closed 0.20 percent lower at 400 on the news but had made gains for two days on the rumour.

"What is important about this transaction is not that it impacts EPS by a franc or even two, but that it signals tangible progress in Havas paying greater attention to shareholder value concerns," Credit Suisse First Boston analyst Chris Renaud said.

* Another big deal which started with a whisper in the morning and quickly echoed round the markets before comfirmation was the sale by luxury goods group LVMH of a seven percent stake in Britain's Guinness Plc, reducing its stake to 14 percent.
LVMH was rewarded for the move with a 3.26 percent rise to 1,551 francs and earlier set a historic high at 1,584 francs.

* Canal Plus managed to dispell some doubts about its digital pay television unit in France by saying that the division, Canalsatellite, had 220,000 subscribers. The share closed 6.67 percent higher at 1,216 francs.
* Other rumours kept hanging around.

* Paribas, up 2.80 percent at 377.80 francs, had no comment on a rumour it was about to sell its Cie Bancaire -- up 3.94 percent at 686 francs -- with the market mentioning General Electric as possible buyer.
* Usinor, down 0.39 percent at 77.60 denied a rumour it wanted to up its stake in Vallourec.

* A spokeswoman for retailer Pinault-Printemps-La Redoute, up 2.72 percent at 2,340 francs, declined comment on a mixed bag of rumours including a possible share swap buy out bid on Rexel or Paribas unit Cetelem.

* At CDR, the state holding charged with selling former Credit Lyonnais assets, there was no comment on another rumour saying it was going to sell its 25 percent stake in Arthemis -- a holding company of Pinault-Printemps-la Redoute -- to the retailer's controlling shareholder Francois Pinault.
* Cap Gemini, up 2.23 percent at 275, continued
its rally despite denial by Debis it wants to raise its stake.
* AXA, up 0.72 percent at 350 francs, said it was paying back early a six percent convertible bond on which there is 3.65 billion francs outstanding.
* Sommer-Allibert closed 3.31 percent higher at 165.30 francs after it said it would sell its bathroom activities.
* Moulinex, down 0.77 percent at 129 francs, said after close that it would issue 5,646,191 shares at 93 francs each for its expected 525 million franc capital increase.
-- Marcel Michelson and Nathalie Meistermann, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452.
